record.original_question: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive, in the sense that every subgroup and every Hausdorff quotient group is reflexive?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive in the sense that all of its subgroups and Hausdorff quotient groups are reflexive?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:
- A topological group is called a pro-Lie group if it is isomorphic, as a topological group, to a projective limit of finite-dimensional real Lie groups. Equivalently, a complete Hausdorff topological group G is pro-Lie if and only if every neighbourhood of the identity contains a closed normal subgroup N such that G/N is a finite-dimensional Lie group.
- For a Hausdorff abelian topological group G, the dual (character) group G^ is the group of continuous homomorphisms G → T (where T = R/Z is the circle group), endowed with the compact-open topology.
- The canonical evaluation map α_G : G → G^^ is defined by α_G(g)(χ) = χ(g) for g ∈ G and χ ∈ G^.
- G is called reflexive (in the sense of Pontryagin–van Kampen) if α_G is a topological isomorphism between G and G^^.
- G is called strongly reflexive if every closed subgroup of G and every Hausdorff quotient group of G is reflexive.

Problem:
Give an intrinsic characterization of those abelian pro-Lie groups G that are strongly reflexive; that is, determine necessary and sufficient structural conditions on an abelian pro-Lie group G under which every closed subgroup of G and every Hausdorff quotient group of G is reflexive.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. It is posed as an open question in surveys on pro-Lie groups, and while related results are known (e.g., every almost connected abelian pro-Lie group is reflexive, and partial strong-reflexivity results exist for certain abelian topological groups), no general intrinsic characterization of strongly reflexive abelian pro-Lie groups has been established in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Pro-Lie Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on pro-Lie groups including the question of which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive.
status_evidence.claim: The strong-reflexivity question for abelian pro-Lie groups is recorded as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Strong Reflexivity of Abelian Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies strong reflexivity for classes of abelian topological groups, providing partial results but not a full characterization for pro-Lie groups.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial strong-reflexivity results exist for abelian topological groups in this generality.

status_evidence.title: A survey on reflexivity of abelian topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing known reflexivity results without a complete characterization for pro-Lie groups.
status_evidence.claim: No general characterization of strongly reflexive abelian pro-Lie groups appears in the survey literature.
